title: Saying goodbye to asm.js
summary: Mozilla's SpiderMonkey JavaScript engine officially deprecates asm.js, a highly optimized JavaScript subset that served as a compilation target for C/C++ code before WebAssembly. The article marks the end of an era for web performance optimization, as WebAssembly has become the superior successor for near-native browser performance.
problem_solved: Legacy asm.js codebase now has a clear path to migrate to modern WebAssembly for better performance and browser support.
why_valuable: Signals the complete transition of high-performance web computing from asm.js to WebAssembly, simplifying the web development ecosystem.
